title: Blue/Green, Canary, and Rolling Deployments
description: Implement production-grade deployment patterns in Azure using App Service slots, Traffic Manager, and load balancer rules.

data.text: While deployment slots handle basic staging needs, larger applications benefit from more advanced patterns. Blue/Green, Canary, and Rolling deployments give you fine-grained control over how new versions reach users.

In a Blue/Green deployment, you maintain two identical production environments. Blue runs the current live version. Green runs the new version. When Green is validated, you redirect traffic from Blue to Green instantly.

data.title: Azure CLI - Configure Traffic Routing with Azure Front Door
data.content: Route traffic between two backends using Azure Front Door.
data.code: az network front-door create --resource-group MyResourceGroup --name MyFrontDoor --backend-address blue-app.azurewebsites.net --backend-address green-app.azurewebsites.net

data.text: Canary deployments route a small percentage of traffic to the new version. If metrics look good, you increase the percentage. If something goes wrong, you route 100 percent back to the stable version.

data.caption: Canary release traffic progression
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    U[Users] -->|5% Canary| N[New Version]
    U -->|95% Stable| O[Old Version]
    N -->|Pass| M[Monitor Metrics]
    M -->|Increase to 25%| N
    M -->|Fail| R[Rollback]
    style N fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#333
    style O fill:#bbdefb,stroke:#333
    style R fill:#ffcdd2,stroke:#333

data.text: Rolling deployments update a subset of instances at a time. Kubernetes Deployments use rolling updates by default, updating pods one by one while keeping the service available.

data.title: YAML - Kubernetes Rolling Update
data.content: A Deployment resource with rolling update strategy.
data.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web-app
          image: myregistry.azurecr.io/web-app:v2
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80

data.title: Azure Front Door Canary
data.text: Azure Front Door Standard/Premium supports weighted traffic routing natively. You can send 5 percent, 25 percent, 50 percent, then 100 percent of traffic to the new backend without any custom code.

data.title: Exercise: Configure a Canary Release
data.description: Use Azure Front Door to route 10 percent of traffic to a new version of your app.
steps: Deploy v2 of your app to a separate App Service
Create an Azure Front Door with two backends (v1 and v2)
Configure a routing rule with 90 percent weight to v1 and 10 percent to v2
Monitor the v2 backend for errors in Application Insights
Increase the weight to 100 percent once confident
data.expectedOutcome: Front Door routing traffic proportionally between two app versions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Blue/Green uses two full environments and swaps traffic instantly
Canary routes a small percentage of traffic to reduce risk
Rolling updates replace instances gradually (default in Kubernetes)
Azure Front Door and App Service slots both support these patterns
data.takeaway: Use Blue/Green for critical applications, Canary for gradual rollouts, and Rolling when running in Kubernetes.
